A.explanation: This is the area under the top force-is-applied curve to the extension axis, not just the thin loop between the two curves.

B.explanation: The loop area equals energy put in during loading minus energy recovered during unloading, which is dissipated as thermal energy in the rubber.

C.explanation: This is the area under the bottom force-is-removed curve to the extension axis, not the area enclosed between loading and unloading.

D.explanation: The two work areas are not added; the recovered work must be subtracted from the input work to leave the net loss.

hints: Look at the axes: force is vertical and extension is horizontal, so work done is the area under each curve to the extension axis.
Compare the top force-is-applied curve with the bottom force-is-removed curve - the top curve encloses a larger area to the axis.
Think what subtracting the smaller unloading area from the larger loading area leaves geometrically on this hysteresis loop.
walkthrough: Identify the graph: vertical axis is force $F$ and horizontal axis is extension $x$ for loading then unloading of rubber.
State the rule: work done in stretching is the area under the $F$ against $x$ curve, given by $W = \int F \, dx$.
Apply to loading: the work done on the rubber as force is applied is the large area under the top curve down to the extension axis.
Apply to unloading: the work done by the rubber as force is removed is the smaller area under the bottom curve down to the extension axis.
Subtract to find net work: input minus recovered equals the thin area enclosed between the two curves, which is energy dissipated as heat due to hysteresis. This is option B.
